e9f62bfba1c6.text: The Windows installer and plaa.exe are signed by Scramble Tools LLC, and the macOS package with its Developer ID, notarized by Apple. Each package is installed, upgraded, run, made to play a video and removed in a clean system before a release goes out. See the install notes for what differs between them, and the release for the sources of the libraries the Windows and macOS packages carry.

4c2329716938.text: Windows releases of plaa are signed by Scramble Tools LLC with <a1>Microsoft Azure Artifact Signing</a1>, and macOS releases with Scramble Tools' Developer ID, notarized by Apple.

1f83be07964a.text: What is signed: only programs built from this project's own source code by its GitHub Actions release workflow: plaa.exe, the libraries it carries and the installers.

840981ec0887.text: Committers and reviewers: the members of the scrambletoolsllc GitHub organization, who review every outside contribution before it is merged.

6263ca064f9a.text: Approvers: the owner of the scrambletoolsllc GitHub organization, who alone can publish a release, and with it a signing.

2d89c53bf0a2.text: Signing runs only in the release workflow, which signs in to Azure without a stored secret. Everyone on the team signs in to GitHub and Azure with two-factor authentication.

b38d6a398de3.text: This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it. plaa goes online only to play the addresses and web pages you open, through yt-dlp for web pages, and to open links you click. On your local network it finds TVs and speakers when you open the Cast menu, serves the file you cast to the one you choose while it plays, and, when you choose a network interface for AVB, takes part in that network. When you use the assistant with a model you added, plaa sends that model your messages and what it asks to see of what plays: to the provider you chose for a cloud model, or to the server you gave for a local model. API keys stay in your system's keychain. Agents reach plaa only through plaa --mcp on your own computer, once you allow them. plaa has no accounts and sends no telemetry. This website sets no cookies and loads nothing from other sites.

325b8765f5de.text: plaa is a free, open source video and audio player, similar to QuickTime Player and IINA, that trims and exports, records, casts to TVs and speakers, sends and listens to AVB and Milan network audio, and lets AI agents such as Claude Code control it over MCP.

3cec564d5325.text: This tour walks through what plaa does, in the order you are likely to meet it. On macOS, use ⌘ where it says Ctrl. The <a1>keyboard shortcuts</a1> are listed at the end, and can be changed in the settings file.

742ca47f4792.text: The screenshots show <a1>Big Buck Bunny</a1>, © 2008 Blender Foundation, under <a2>CC BY 3.0</a2>.

167c4009085d.text: Started on its own, plaa offers to open a file or an address, or to record. Open a file with Ctrl+O, from the file manager's Open With, from the command line (plaa film.mkv), or by dropping it on a window. Open Address (Ctrl+U) takes a stream or a web page, and offers the addresses opened lately again.

fffa3294da8b.text: Each file plays in a window of its own, and there is one running plaa: a file opened again from the file manager or the command line goes to the running one, as files opened from Finder do on macOS. To have video and sound files open in plaa, use Make Default in <a1>Settings</a1>.

8a60f2cfa0bc.text: The toolbar and the playback controls float over the picture and slide away once the pointer rests or leaves the window, and come back when it moves. The floating bars button docks them above and below the picture instead, and on a narrow window the tools that do not fit go into the More menu.

caab4aa19422.text: Pointing at the timeline shows a picture from there, its time and its chapter; dragging it moves the picture with the handle, exactly. The arrow keys skip 5 seconds, J and L 10, and the comma and period keys step a frame. Speed goes from a quarter to three times, keeping the sound's pitch, and the volume and full screen are at the right of the controls.

5a8ed52dd42d.text: Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom in on the picture at the pointer, up to 16 times, and dragging it looks around. Picture in picture (Ctrl+Shift+P) keeps a small window over the others in a corner. plaa resumes each file where you left off, keeps the screen on while video plays, and keeps the computer awake while sound does.

18a188fe3b03.text: Video is decoded on the graphics card where it can be, 8K at 60 frames a second included, and drawn by plaa's own shader: BT.601, BT.709 and BT.2020 colors, 8 to 16 bits, HDR10 and HLG tone mapped for an ordinary screen, and phone videos turned upright. The sound keeps in step with the picture by the output device's own clock.

a4828ced06bc.text: plaa picks the audio and subtitle tracks in the languages Settings prefer, and the menu at the right of the controls changes them. It shows text subtitles (SubRip, WebVTT, MP4 text and more), ASS and SSA styled as made through libass, and Blu-ray, DVD and DVB picture subtitles. Subtitle files beside the video, such as Film.en.srt, or in a Subs folder, are offered too.

a82a7e7d8874.text: A file's chapters are marked on the timeline and listed in a menu, and Page Up and Page Down move between them. Loop (Ctrl+L) plays the file over and over; B marks where an A-B loop starts, and B again where it ends.

761e4c8c76ad.text: plaa plays HTTP, HLS, DASH, RTSP and SRT addresses. Streams read ahead, and wait to read on rather than stutter over a slow network, marking on the timeline how far they have read; a spinner shows while they wait.

1501342093ab.text: With <a1>yt-dlp</a1> installed, plaa also plays the videos on web pages such as YouTube's, with their titles, channels, chapters and thumbnails, and a web playlist becomes a plaa playlist. A stream or web video plays in the quality that fits your screen, or the one chosen from the quality menu, which also offers the sound alone.

ff93c5f1912b.text: Files opened or dropped together play one after another, as do M3U and PLS lists, and in Settings plaa can list the other files in the opened file's folder. The playlist (Ctrl+P) shows beside the picture; P and N go to the previous and next item, and the next one plays when one ends.

cc3e703d5fa6.text: A sound file shows its cover, title, artist and album, with the spectrum of what you hear below them, as bars that rise with it and fall back slowly, or the file's waveform from start to end, the part played in the accent color, which a click or a drag seeks along.

4ca6fd3d67d0.text: Or choose Prism from the visualizer menu: a scene in three dimensions that fills the window and moves with the music, a lace orb around a core that swells on each beat, ringed by glass shards rising with the spectrum, over a rippling grid of light.

09af2b7ec14b.text: The inspector (Ctrl+I) shows what a file is made of: its name, folder, size, format, duration and bit rate, its tags, and each of its streams, with the video's codec, size, frame rate and pixel format and how it is decoded, and the sound's codec, rate, channels and language.

b1936c4ed84f.text: Trim (Ctrl+T) shows the file as a strip of pictures with a handle at each end, and plays the part kept over and over while you move them; I and O set them to where it plays. Split (Ctrl+Y) cuts the file into clips at the playhead, which you can drag into another order, trim one by one, or remove with Delete. Rotate and flip (Ctrl+Shift+L, R, H and V) turn the picture, and undo and redo cover every step.

3f7dbb4e3ccd.text: The edit plays as it will be, clip after clip without a gap. Nothing changes in the file: the edit is kept until you export it, and closing the window with an edit not exported asks first.

16262e5c9802.text: Ask the assistant, or an agent, and the edit can mix files too: put in a part of another file, or play another file's sound or picture over a part, such as music under a video or a voice over it, or make a part silent or black. The clips show each file's pictures, and the edit plays and exports as it will be.

14143300b3e3.text: They can also put the picture or the sound through FFmpeg's filters, for all of it or a part: black and white, color and contrast, a crop, sharpening, a title, less noise or an even loudness. plaa checks each filter before it runs, and the result plays at once.

9dc8ca2429f1.text: Export (Ctrl+E) saves what plays, as edited, as H.264, HEVC or AV1 with AAC sound, at the file's own size or smaller. plaa encodes on the graphics card where it can (NVENC, AMF, Quick Sync, VAAPI or VideoToolbox) and on the processor otherwise, and the dialog says which. HDR video keeps its colors in HEVC and AV1.

2cde4cf09d8f.text: Sound only saves the sound alone: AAC, MP3 or Opus at a bit rate you choose, or lossless as FLAC, ALAC or WAV in 16 or 24 bits.

6fe776ee86a3.text: Record Sound (Ctrl+Shift+N) records a microphone, or what the computer plays where the system offers it, with a level meter. Louder takes a quiet input up to 30 dB higher, kept for each input, and Level automatically evens the level out. Space starts and stops; once it stops, plaa asks what to name the recording, then plays it, ready to trim and export.

ede4cf909ce8.text: Record Screen (Ctrl+Alt+N) records a screen or a window, or on Linux a region, with the pointer, and the sound of a microphone or of what the computer plays if you like, on the graphics card's encoder at 24 to 120 pictures a second. Recording a screen, plaa's own windows stay out of it on macOS; elsewhere the recording window steps aside, and the red dot in the tray on Linux, or opening plaa again, stops it.

1000efaffc1a.text: Record Camera (Ctrl+Alt+M) records a camera, as QuickTime Player's New Movie Recording does, its picture shown mirrored while it records. Sound recordings go to Music, and screen and camera recordings to Videos (Movies on macOS), unless Settings choose other folders.

04a5d9d5c3ea.text: The Cast menu looks for Chromecasts and for TVs, speakers and programs that play DLNA on your network as it opens. Choose one, and plaa serves the file to it, or hands it the stream's address; plaa's own controls and timeline then play, pause and seek it there. When casting stops, the window goes on from where it got to.

005aec8d8b05.text: plaa takes part in AVB and Milan networks, the kind that links professional speakers, amplifiers and audio interfaces. In Settings, Network, choose the wired interface the network is on. With Send what plays on, plaa becomes a Milan talker of its own on Linux, and sends through the Mac's own AVB entity on macOS: the sound of the window last played goes out as a stream on the network's clock, which any Milan controller can connect.

bcaca47349b5.text: The Network Audio button lists the listeners that can play plaa's sound, each with one button, and how the one chosen takes its stream, kept up to date as other controllers change it. The Connect menu, beside Open, lists the talkers plaa can listen to, and plays the one chosen in a window, as a file plays.

5090f28c007d.text: Where the switch has no AVB, plaa falls back to AVB Lite and sends each listener, up to five, a copy of its own. On Linux plaa keeps network time with ptp4l, starting its own service where nothing else runs one, and shares the network's reservations with triib's entity service where it runs. The <a1>README</a1> says what each system needs.

ca9d0cf44e78.text: The assistant button opens a chat panel beside what plays. Ask about it, and the assistant looks with plaa's own tools, at the status, the file's streams, its pictures at any time, how loud it is and its subtitles, and plays, pauses, seeks, changes the sound or edits it for you, each step shown as it goes.

bcfe366f6e93.text: Use a local model that stays on your computer, such as Ollama's or one behind an OpenAI-compatible server, or a cloud model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google with your own key, kept in the system's keychain. Add models in Settings, Assistant; they are shared with the other Scramble Tools apps, such as <a1>prev</a1>.

c360200a4f5b.text: Agents such as Claude Code can see what plays, read any part of it, and control and edit the plaa you are using, through MCP. Add plaa to an agent as an MCP server that runs plaa --mcp; for Claude Code:

f112d44f5eca.text: The first time an agent connects, plaa asks whether to let it in. Settings, Agents, turns outside control off, lists the agents allowed, and has a switch for each kind of tool, seeing what plays, controlling playback, opening files or closing windows, and editing or exporting, that makes plaa ask before an agent's call runs. Every edit shows in the window as it is made, and undo takes it back. plaa bundles no model and listens on no network.

aa4b2a4fabe0.text: Settings (Ctrl+,) has seven tabs. Appearance chooses light or dark, the system's accent color or one of plaa's, and how the floating controls look and when they hide. Playback has hardware decoding, the sound output, resuming, folder playlists, the streams' quality, yt-dlp, and Make Default, which makes plaa the system's default app for video and sound files. Storage chooses the folders recordings and saved frames go to; Network, the AVB interface; Language, plaa's language and the languages tracks are chosen by; Agents and Assistant, what the previous sections describe.

2d1b9732fc3c.text: None of its own: plaa goes online only to play the addresses and web pages you open and to open links you click; on your local network it finds TVs and speakers as the Cast menu opens, and takes part in the AVB network you choose. No accounts, no telemetry

816fb5946fd6.text: Only those you allow, through plaa --mcp; no bundled model. What an agent sees goes to the model it uses

8636174fad23.text: Talks only to the model you add: a local model stays on your computer, and a cloud model gets what it asks to see. API keys stay in the system keychain
